hero: A small pediatric nephrology clinic room in Batangas. A sixteen-year-old Filipino girl in a school uniform sits beside a pediatric nephrologist; both look at her phone, which shows a medicine reminder screen. A pill organizer and her school bag are on the desk. Through the half-open door, her mother waits in the corridor. Afternoon light, respectful, encouraging mood, no text.

figures.teaches: The six common causes of a rising creatinine in a pediatric graft and the first clue and test for each.
figures.content: Center: kidney labeled 'Graft'. Six spokes: 'Dehydration' (Diarrhea, vomiting / Rehydrate, repeat); 'Tacrolimus high' (Tremor, interaction / Trough level); 'Rejection' (Low or swinging levels / Antibodies, biopsy); 'BK virus' (Often silent / Plasma BK load); 'Obstruction' (Valve bladder / Ultrasound); 'Recurrence' (Proteinuria, hemolysis / Urine protein). Footer: 'Often more than one'.

figures.teaches: When graft-failure risk peaks and how adherence support and transition steps line up with age.
figures.content: Horizontal timeline ages 12 to 25. Curve rising to a peak labeled 'Peak at 19: 6.6 per 100 person-years' and band labeled '17-24: hazard ratio 1.20'. Above the timeline, adherence tools: 'Teen chooses reminder', 'Coach reviews data', 'One barrier at a time'. Below, transition steps: '12-14 Start talking', 'Seen alone', 'Names own medicines', 'Joint visit', 'First adult visit confirmed'.

card: A teenager's hand holding a phone with a pill organizer and a school notebook nearby on a desk, warm light, no text.
